question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics as a core Doctor feature before the MCP-ownership prerequisite and RFC have landed?
rationale: The implementation may be technically viable, but accepting a new core lifecycle-management and diagnostics surface is a product and ownership choice that tests cannot resolve.

options.title: Pause for core ownership decision
options.body: Keep this stacked PR open but do not advance merge review until an owner confirms the RFC and core ownership of the Claw lifecycle surface.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core experiment
options.body: Confirm core ownership, land the prerequisite ownership slices in order, and require current-head integrated runtime proof before merging this diagnostics layer.

options.title: Move lifecycle orchestration outside core
options.body: Decline the core experiment and redirect any optional lifecycle workflow to a supported external package only if existing extension seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Pause for core ownership decision
recommendation.body: Keep this stacked PR open but do not advance merge review until an owner confirms the RFC and core ownership of the Claw lifecycle surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline indicates direct involvement in the maintained experimental Claws stack, while the decision is product direction rather than a mechanical code repair.
